name: Saint Elizabeth of Portugal
history: A princess of Aragon, named after her great-aunt Saint Elizabeth of Hungary, who was married young to King Denis of Portugal. She bore his infidelities with patience, cared for the poor and sick, and more than once made peace between her husband and their rebellious son. Widowed, she lived as a Franciscan tertiary beside the Poor Clares at Coimbra.
life: Elizabeth was married at about twelve to King Denis, a capable ruler but an unfaithful husband. She kept a regular life of prayer at court, founded hospitals, a shelter for abandoned women and foundling homes, and brought up the king’s children by other women with kindness. When her son Afonso rose in arms against his father, she worked tirelessly for reconciliation, and in 1323, tradition says, rode out between the two armies to stop the battle. After Denis died in 1325 she made a pilgrimage to Compostela, then lived simply in a house beside the convent of Poor Clares she had founded at Coimbra. In 1336, though old and ill, she travelled in summer heat to make peace between her son, now king, and the king of Castile. She died at Estremoz soon after and was canonised in 1625. Portugal remembers her as the Holy Queen.
prayerTo: Saint Elizabeth, queen and peacemaker, you answered unfaithfulness with patience and war with reconciliation. Pray for marriages under strain, for families at odds, and for all who rule. Give me the courage to step between those who quarrel, and the humility to begin with myself. Amen.
penance: Do something kind today for a family member you find difficult, and pray for a marriage you know is struggling.
meditation: She rode out between her husband and her son. Where could you be a bridge rather than take a side?
prayer: Most merciful God, Who among other admirable gifts, endowed blessed Queen Elizabeth with the special grace of calming the tumult of war; grant by her intercession that, after the peace for which we humbly pray, we may attain everlasting happiness. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
